sources.entry: Poirot - Companion app for browsing Claude Code sessions, reviewing diffs, and rerunning commands. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/LeonardoCardoso/Poirot) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
Poirot - A macOS app for browsing Claude Code sessions, exploring diffs, and re-running commands. Reads local transcripts, runs offline, open source.

summary.one_liner: Poirot is a native macOS SwiftUI companion app for browsing Claude Code sessions from local transcripts, exploring their diffs, and re-running commands.
summary.what_it_does: Poirot reads JSONL transcripts from ~/.claude/projects/ and presents Claude Code sessions grouped by project, with timestamps, model info, and token counts. Each session opens into a conversation timeline with markdown rendering, syntax-highlighted inline diffs for Edit tool blocks, collapsible tool and thinking blocks, and Bash output with exit status. Analytics cover token consumption, cost breakdowns, and model distribution, and a live usage-limit view shows 5-hour and 7-day rate-limit gauges. The app also browses slash commands, skills, MCP server status, sub-agents, plugins, hooks, plans, memory files, prompt history, and debug logs, with a ⌘K fuzzy search across them. Sessions can be exported as Markdown or PDF, and clicking a Bash command copies it or opens it in a chosen terminal.
use_cases: Review what Claude Code did in past sessions
Inspect file edits and diffs made by Claude Code
Re-run or copy Bash commands from a previous session
Track token usage and cost of Claude Code
Search across Claude Code sessions, prompts, and config
Export a Claude Code session to Markdown or PDF
how_to_run: git clone (repository URL), then cd Poirot
open Poirot.xcodeproj and press ⌘R in Xcode
notable: Runs fully local with no login, tracking, or analytics; reads Claude Code's existing OAuth token for usage limits
Native SwiftUI app under 6 MB that works offline
Universal ⌘K search across sessions, commands, skills, memory, plans, and more
Lazy loading of projects in configurable batches
Extensible ProviderDescribing protocol intended for multi-LLM support
caveats: Requires macOS 15.0 or later and Xcode 16.0 or later to build
README describes the project as early, with a roadmap tracked on the issues page
Usage-limit gauges depend on the OAuth token Claude Code already stores
keywords: see what my ai assistant did
